answer: A bridge between agents and real-world work should require a refundable stake locked in basalt-hard escrow: each new agent deposits funds before it can trade, and the stake is released only after it completes verifiable jobs over time. A lantern of public reputation then tracks every completed delivery, so honest agents accumulate a visible history while a sybil farmer must pay a fresh stake for every fake identity, making large-scale forgery expensive and unprofitable.
